mike (runtime): Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a concrete plan for rollback heuristics + a circuit-style fallback for model rollouts. Thinking a short thread to capture tradeoffs and next steps :thinking_face:

sara (platform): Yep. The RFC covered goals at a high level, but we left the exact signals and the interface between rollout controller -> router ambiguous.

jordan (sre): Signals we can provide reliably: per-route error_rate, 95p latency, infra OOMs, and node capacity. Any heuristics must be resilient to noisy traffic.

leila (ml): Also add quality regressions (eval-based) and a semantic similarity fallback for hallucination spikes. We can publish a small prompt-based eval stream from prod sampling.

mike (runtime): Proposal sketch:
1) Local fast heuristics in router: short-window thresholds (error_rate > 3% OR p95 > 800ms over 2m) -> immediate circuit to fallback variant (smaller model or cached response).
2) Controller-level rollback: sustained degradations over 10m with alerting -> mark canary unhealthy and trigger automated rollback.
3) Safety net: if metric is ambiguous (e.g. p95 spike but low error_rate), route fractionally (50%) to fallback for 5m while telemetry collects.

sara (platform): Interface boundary idea: rollout controller emits decisions as policy blobs with fields: target_fraction, fallback_variant, reason, ttl. Router subscribes and enforces. That keeps router dumb and fast.

mike (runtime): Agree. Need the policy schema to be tiny — router only needs: "type", "target_fraction", "fallback_variant", and "circuit_state". Everything else can be metadata for the controller/console.

jordan (sre): Tradeoffs: short-window router decisions reduce blast radius but increase flapping risk. We'll need hysteresis and cooldown. Suggest exponential backoff for re-open attempts and a single-ticket alert on open -> closed transition.

leila (ml): For quality signals, we can't rely solely on real-time labels. Suggested hybrid: fast automatic checks (semantic similarity, perplexity proxy) + deferred offline evals that can trigger controller-to-human review.

mike (runtime): Example heuristic config (proto-yaml):
```yaml
- name: cpu_and_latency_guard
  trigger:
    error_rate_pct: 3
    p95_ms: 800
    window_s: 120
  action:
    type: circuit
    fallback_variant: lightweight-v1
    cooldown_s: 300
    reopen_strategy: exponential_backoff
```

sara (platform): Love it. Also we should version these blobs and store them with rollout history so we can audit why a route tripped. Make them immutable once attached to a rollout.

jordan (sre): Ops automation: when router trips a circuit, emit a short event to incident stream and create a synthetic metric (circuit_opened). We can hook automatic paging thresholds to that.

leila (ml): Long-term refactor: split "fallback policy" from "rollout policy". Right now rollout blob includes fallback info; we should extract fallback into its own resource that can be shared across rollouts (e.g., fallback to model-family X or to cached-response behavior).

mike (runtime): Implementation plan + owners:
- Router changes (fast policy apply + circuit): mike -> small PR to add policy fields + cooldown logic (2w).
- Policy storage + versioning: sara -> API + console changes (3w).
- Telemetry hooks + incident events: jordan -> metrics + alert rules (1w).
- Quality probes + offline eval pipeline: leila -> sample exporter + eval job (3w).

sara (platform): Dev note: make sure fallback policy includes "cost cap" and "token soft-limit" so router can prefer cheaper fallbacks under high unit-cost.

jordan (sre): Edge case: cross-route cascading — if many routes fallback to same variant, that variant might become overloaded. Add capacity-aware gating in controller: if fallback pool utilization > 70% then degrade to cached or synthetic responses.

mike (runtime): Good call. We'll add a small admission check in the controller: query pool_util and swap fallback_variant -> cached if above threshold.

leila (ml): One more tradeoff: aggressive automatic rollback reduces time to fix but increases ops churn. Recommend conservative defaults (3% err short-circuit, 10m sustained rollback) and make them editable per-customer.

sara (platform): Action item: I'll draft the policy schema and an RFC appendix documenting the router->controller API and versioning rules. Posting timeline by EOD tomorrow.

mike (runtime): Thanks. I'll start the router prototype and post a demo log snippet in this thread once I have it. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: mike triggered deploy runtime/circuit-guard:branch-42 at 1779004500 :rocket:

jordan (sre): Noted deploy, monitoring the synthetic metrics stream. If we see >1 circuit_opened in 5m, I'll escalate.

mike (runtime): Updated plan: prototype -> test on internal staging, then a week-long canary with 1% traffic, monitor both infra and eval signals, then slowly ramp.

sara (platform): Solid. Summarizing: short-window router circuits + controller-sustained rollback + policy blobs + fallback resource + capacity admission. I'll own schema + console bits.

mike (runtime): Perfect. Closing this thread for now; will reopen with the RFC appendix link.
